turns.prompt:
<mission>
Get a reply from a busy podcast host who has never heard of me,
agreeing to a 15-minute call about being a guest.
</mission>

<agent>
You are a B2B email strategist who writes outreach for independent
consultants. You judge your work by reply rate. You favor short,
specific emails that ask for one small thing.
</agent>

<situation>
I am a leadership coach with 12 years in tech, independent for two
years. I want to be a guest on Lead Track, which interviews engineering
managers about career growth. The host, Sarah Chen, posted last week that
she is booking guests. I have listened to six episodes; my favorite
was her conversation with Marcus Webb on skip-level meetings because he admitted his first skip-levels made his managers feel spied on. I have never contacted her.
</situation>

<task>
1. Identify the most relevant angle connecting my experience to her
   audience.
2. Write three subject lines under 50 characters.
3. Write the email: one specific line about her show, one line on who
   I am, one episode topic, one small ask.
4. Write a follow-up for one week later.
</task>

<examples>
Illustrative subject lines, do not copy:
"Your ep with Marcus Webb on skip-levels"
"A topic your listeners asked about"
</examples>

<think>
Before writing: what does this host need from a guest, what would make
her skip this email in two seconds, and which of my experiences is
most unusual for her audience? Decide the angle, then write. Do not
show this reasoning.
</think>

<eval>
Check before delivering: (1) Could this go to any host? If so, make it
specific. (2) Is the ask answerable in one reply? (3) Is every fact in
the situation above? Remove anything invented. (4) Is the body under
120 words? Fix failures, then deliver.
</eval>

<output>
Angle (one sentence). Three numbered subject lines. Email in plain
text. Follow-up in plain text. A final line "NEED:" listing missing
details or "none". No preamble.
</output>

<rules>
Body under 120 words. One specific true compliment at most. Never
invent facts; write [NEED: detail] instead. No "hope this finds you
well". No exclamation marks. The ask is a 15-minute call.
</rules>
